source.title_on_document: Human–GenAI collaboration across creative phases: Cognitive mechanisms shaping novelty and usefulness

supplement.where: The paper cites no supplementary material or online appendix. Appendices A to I (interview profiles, interview questions, coding framework, task texts, manipulation materials, scale items) are inside this PDF, pp. 11-14.
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text; no extra statistics are referenced outside this PDF. The Study 3 preregistration is at https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf.

paper_design_summary: Four studies on Chinese-language creative tasks. Study 1 interviews 20 creative professionals. Studies 2a (42 students) and 2b (44 students) are within-person lab experiments in which each student writes two product proposals, one with the SparkDesk LLM allowed in one phase (idea generation in 2a, idea elaboration in 2b) and one without AI, in randomized order; three marketing experts rate novelty and usefulness. Study 3 (198 full-time employees) is an online 2 x 2 between-subjects experiment that randomizes whether ChatGPT is available in the idea generation or the idea elaboration phase of an advertising-copy task, crossed with a high versus low perceived-GenAI-intelligence news manipulation; experts rate novelty and usefulness.

outcomes.name: Novelty of final proposal
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Consensual assessment technique: three marketing experts, blind to purpose, hypotheses, and conditions, rated whether the proposal had a high degree of novelty (7-point); average of the three used. ICC2 H condition = 0.82, GenAI condition = 0.85.

contrasts.reported: Table 1 (N = 42): Novelty (GenAI condition) M = 6.05, SD = 0.59; Novelty (H condition) M = 5.44, SD = 0.55; correlation between the two = 0.14. No direct test of the novelty difference is printed. Indirect effect of GenAI collaboration on novelty through cognitive flexibility = 0.17, 95% CI = [0.033, 0.341] (5000 bootstraps).

outcomes.name: Usefulness of final proposal
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same three marketing experts; usefulness = potential for practical implementation, solving real problems, creating value; average of three. ICC2 H condition = 0.87, GenAI condition = 0.82.

contrasts.reported: Table 1 (N = 42): USEN (GenAI condition) M = 5.37, SD = 0.52; USEN (H condition) M = 5.21, SD = 0.45; correlation between the two = -0.06. No test of the difference is printed.

eligibility.reason: Study 3 randomly assigns 198 analyzed employees (205 recruited) between two AI configurations (ChatGPT in the idea generation phase vs. in the idea elaboration phase), with expert-rated novelty and usefulness of the written output; this is an ai_design contrast with no no-AI arm. Studies 2a (42 analyzed) and 2b (44 analyzed) are randomized-order within-person AI vs. no-AI experiments but fall below 50 people.

one_line_finding: In Study 3 (N = 198), having ChatGPT in the elaboration phase rather than the generation phase correlates with lower expert-rated novelty (r = -0.30) and higher usefulness (r = 0.42) (p. 8, Table 3); in the small within-person Studies 2a/2b, AI-assisted proposals had higher mean novelty (6.05 vs 5.44, N = 42) and usefulness (5.89 vs 5.49, N = 44) than unassisted ones (Tables 1-2, pp. 6-7).
open_questions: Study 3 reports no arm means for novelty or usefulness; the only total-effect statistic is the point-biserial correlation of the phase dummy with each outcome in Table 3 (convertible with N = 198 and the 0.49 share in the elaboration arm). Is that acceptable for extraction, or do we need to contact the authors?

In Study 2a and in the generation-phase arm of Study 3, AI was available in the first 10 minutes but barred (Study 2a, Appendix E) during the elaboration phase in which the final scored proposal was written. I coded ai_available_when_produced = mixed and question = with_ai, because AI ideas feed the same task's output; a stricter reading of the codebook could call it after_ai.
Study 3 does not state explicitly that ChatGPT was unavailable in the non-assigned phase; the custom system 'guided participants' interactions with GenAI during specific creative phases' (p. 7).

For the ai_design contrast in Study 3 neither arm is a default configuration. I set treatment = elaboration-phase AI following the Table 3 coding (1 = idea elaboration); the paper codes the novelty mediation the other way (1 = idea generation).
Study 3 per-cell counts and the timing of the 7 exclusions are not reported.
Studies 2a/2b report no direct test of the AI vs. no-AI difference in novelty or usefulness, only means, SDs, and within-person correlations plus indirect effects.
notes: Phase coding is inconsistent inside Study 3: Table 3 and the text on p. 8 code collaboration phase 1 = idea elaboration, the H3 mediation codes 1 = idea generation, and the H5 mediation codes 1 = idea elaboration. The perceived-GenAI-intelligence factor is a framing manipulation (news article plus recall), not a different AI configuration; the paper reports its effect only on self-reported cognitive overload (F(1, 194) = 5.06, Fig. 2, p. 9) and through moderated mediation indices (H6a INDEX = 0.14, 95% CI [-0.018, 0.313] for novelty; H7a INDEX = 0.26, 95% CI [0.019, 0.516] for usefulness), so I coded no output contrast for it. Cognitive flexibility and cognitive overload are self-reported mediators, not output outcomes. The Study 3 manipulation check compares generation and elaboration arms (t(196) = 28.63). Study 3 G*Power target was 146 participants. Study 1 (N = 20 interviews) has no outcomes scored on output. The Study 2 tasks list four products (Task A/B/C/D) but the paper does not say which two each sub-study used.
